subject.title: Transcript entry id is stripped before plugin conversation hooks, leaving no stable per-message identifier

question: Should the plugin hook contract expose the persisted transcript record ID, and if so should it be a documented field under the existing __openclaw namespace rather than a new top-level message property?
rationale: The implementation is likely small, but choosing and documenting a durable plugin-facing data contract is a maintainer API decision.

options.title: Expose a namespaced entry ID
options.body: Add and document __openclaw.entryId on hook conversation messages at the shared history-loader boundary, retaining all current fields.

options.title: Use a top-level field
options.body: Expose entryId directly on hook messages if maintainers want this identity to be part of the general conversation-message contract.

options.title: Keep the contract unchanged
options.body: Decline the new identifier and document the supported plugin-level correlation approach, accepting that it cannot provide a stable persisted-record key.

recommendation.title: Expose a namespaced entry ID
recommendation.body: Add and document __openclaw.entryId on hook conversation messages at the shared history-loader boundary, retaining all current fields.

likelyOwner.reason: Available feature history connects solstead to the lifecycle-hook conversation-history surface where this contract decision belongs.
